entities.name: Abraham Woyna
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abraham Woyna (1569–1649) was a Polish Catholic bishop who served as auxiliary bishop of Vilnius (Wilno) and later as Bishop of Inflanty (Livonia), navigating the complex ecclesiastical landscape of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the Counter-Reformation. Born into the Polish nobility, he pursued an ecclesiastical career in the eastern reaches of the Commonwealth, where Polish Catholicism, Lithuanian paganism's lingering heritage, Orthodox Christianity, and Lutheranism all competed for influence.

The Diocese of Vilnius was one of the most important sees in the eastern Catholic world — Vilnius was the capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and a city of extraordinary religious pluralism, with Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, Jewish, and Tatar communities coexisting under the Commonwealth's relatively tolerant framework. The Jesuit-led Counter-Reformation was actively working to reinforce Catholic identity among the Lithuanian nobility and reclaim communities that had drifted toward Lutheranism or Calvinism.

Woyna's episcopate in the Diocese of Inflanty (corresponding to modern Latvia and Estonia) engaged the particularly challenging situation of a region that had been Lutheran since the Reformation, where the Catholic minority maintained its faith in a predominantly Protestant environment. His ministry represented the Counter-Reformation's sustained effort to maintain Catholic presence in the Baltic territories.
